newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghanistan's Taleban claim advance north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghanistan's Taleban claim advance north of Kabul.

text.p: Forces of the purist Islamic Taleban on Thursday took a small town north of the Afghan capital Kabul, according to a Taleban commander close to the front line.

"We captured Mir Batcha Kot (17 miles or 27 km north of Kabul) and Gul Dara this morning. Mir Batcha Kot is still under heavy fire, the opposition put up strong resistance," said Taleban commander Mullah Abdul Manan on Thursday morning.
There was no independent confirmation of his comments and Manan would not allow journalists to visit the areas he said had been captured, saying that the area was still too dangerous.
The sound of heavy artillery barrages and rocket fire was clearly audible in Kabul itself on Wednesday night and into the early hours of Thursday morning.
Manan said that Mir Batcha Kot had been captured at 9 a.m. (0430 GMT) after the Taleban repulsed an opposition attack.
"They (the opposition) launched an offensive last night and again this morning, (and) after they were exhausted the Taleban forces pushed forward," said Manan.
The opposition took Mir Batcha Kot in a rapid advance over four days last week. The Taleban were pushed back from the foothills of the Hindu Kush mountains to within 15 miles (24 km) of Kabul.
The advance put the opposition within rocket range of the Afghan capital for the first time in nine months.

If the Taleban claims of an advance are confirmed, Thursday's action would be the first time that the front lines on the two main roads leading north from Kabul have changed since the opposition advance.
Thursday's action came on the same day as the opposition postponed a meeting with the United Nations special envoy to Afghanistan, Norbert Holl.
Holl was supposed to meet opposition leaders in their stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif in northern Afghanistan on Thursday.

U.N. officials in the town said that the meeting was postponed because General Abdul Malik, one of the leaders of the tripartite alliance and a representative of Ahmed Shah Masood, another of the leaders, could not be in Mazar on Thursday.
"We have been told that General Abdul Malik and a delegate representing Masood cannot be in Mazar on Thursday, (and) the talks have been rescheduled for Friday," said the officials.
